newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa aiming for $20 billion in revenues.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa aiming for $20 billion in revenues.

text.p: Aluminum Co of America is aiming to reach $20 billion in annual revenues by 2000, Chairman Paul O'Neill said Friday.
"We think we can do this," he told shareholders at the annual meeting.
After the meeting, O'Neill told reporters that acquisitions will be an "important part" of the revenue growth.
"Acquisitions will be an important part, but they won't be the only part," he said. "We have 22 (business units) and every one is doing something to help with (the revenue growth.")
He said revenue growth would also be partially achieved through productivity improvements and employing new technology.
Last year, Alcoa posted annual revenues slightly over $13 billion. O'Neill said revenues this year should be between $13 and $14 billion.

Alcoa has made a string of acquisitions, some of them international, over the past several years. The company recently announced it plans to buy some aluminum rolling operations from a competitor, Reynolds Metals Co.
"That will add $700 to $800 million (in revenues,") O'Neill said.
